_meta.description: Reference knowledge for BHW community comment generation. Each category has facts, tips, and common mistakes that can be turned into genuinely helpful replies. Add more entries to improve comment quality. OpenClaw picks the most relevant entries for each thread.
_meta.instructions: Add new categories freely. Each entry has: 'tip' (the actual knowledge), 'context' (when it applies), 'tags' (keywords for matching).

web_scraping.description: Web scraping, crawlers, data extraction, Puppeteer, Playwright, Selenium, Scrapy

tips.tip: Rotating proxies alone won't save you if your User-Agent and browser fingerprint look robotic. Use puppeteer-real-browser or Playwright with stealth plugin to randomize canvas, WebGL, and timezone fingerprints.

Scrapy's DOWNLOAD_DELAY combined with AUTOTHROTTLE_ENABLED dynamically adjusts your crawl speed based on server response times. Set AUTOTHROTTLE_TARGET_CONCURRENCY to 0.5 for residential-looking traffic patterns.

For JavaScript-heavy sites, a simple headless browser is overkill if you only need data from the initial HTML. Intercept XHR/fetch calls with page.on('response') in Puppeteer to grab the raw JSON the frontend fetches — much faster than parsing rendered HTML.
Residential proxies from ISPs are significantly harder to detect than datacenter proxies. If you're getting blocked, the proxy type is usually the first thing to change before tweaking any code.

When a site uses CAPTCHA, look for the API endpoint being called directly rather than rendering the page. Many sites validate tokens server-side but the actual data endpoint has no CAPTCHA protection.

Set realistic random delays — not just between page loads but between mouse events, keystrokes and form submissions. Most modern bot detection measures the timing variance between UI events, not just request rate.

For large-scale scraping, run Chrome in a persistent context with a real Chrome user profile. The browser will accumulate cookies, history, and cache that make fingerprints indistinguishable from a real user.

seo.description: Search engine optimization, rankings, backlinks, on-page SEO, technical SEO

tips.tip: Core Web Vitals (LCP, INP, CLS) directly affect rankings in 2025. LCP is almost always a server response time or render-blocking resource issue — fix your TTFB first before touching images.
Internal linking is one of the most underrated ranking levers. A well-structured silo with topic clusters and tight internal linking passes PageRank more effectively than dozens of new backlinks.

For local SEO, consistent NAP (Name, Address, Phone) across all citations makes a bigger difference than most people expect. An inconsistency in a single major citation site can suppress the Google Business Profile map pack ranking.
E-E-A-T signals are increasingly important for YMYL niches. Author pages with real credentials and bio links to external publications carry significantly more weight than generic content.
Structured data (JSON-LD schema markup) doesn't directly boost rankings but dramatically increases CTR by adding rich results in SERP. FAQ schema is the fastest win for informational pages.

Programmatic SEO works when your database has unique data that can't be easily replicated. Thin pages with templated content penalize your whole domain — each page must offer a unique enough variation to justify indexing.

When recovering from a Google penalty, start by identifying which update hit you using a timeline correlation tool. Most HCU (Helpful Content Update) recoveries require architectural changes to the site, not just content rewrites.

wordpress.description: WordPress development, plugins, themes, WooCommerce, performance, security

tips.tip: WP_CRON is notoriously unreliable on low-traffic sites because it only fires when a page loads. Replace it with a real server cron job: add `define('DISABLE_WP_CRON', true)` to wp-config.php and set up a 5-minute server cron calling wp-cron.php.

Before any custom post type or taxonomy query, always check you're using pre_get_posts on the main query rather than a new WP_Query loop. Secondary loops skip the main query cache and hit the DB every time.

For WooCommerce stores doing significant volume, move session storage from default PHP sessions to database sessions, and put a transient cache layer in front of product meta queries. The default implementation hits the DB on every cart action.

Dequeuing unused scripts per page type is faster than any caching plugin. Use conditional tags (is_front_page, is_woocommerce, is_singular) in wp_enqueue_scripts to only load what each page type actually needs.
For WordPress REST API integrations, use application passwords (built-in since WP 5.6) instead of plugins like JWT Auth. They're nonce-protected, revokable per device, and simpler to audit.

The fastest way to find the bottleneck in a slow WordPress site is Query Monitor plugin in development mode. Sort queries by execution time — 90% of the time a single bad meta_query with no index is the culprit.

automation.description: Task automation, bots, workflow automation, RPA, Make/Zapier, n8n, scripts

tips.tip: When automating web workflows that require login, cookies are much more reliable than re-authenticating each run. Serialize and save your authenticated cookies after first login, load them on subsequent runs before making any requests.

n8n self-hosted is dramatically cheaper than Make or Zapier for high-volume automations. The workflow logic is near-identical, and you own the data. Run it on a $5–10 VPS and it handles thousands of executions per day.

Error handling in automation is where most pipelines fail. Every step that makes an external call (API, scrape, email) needs a retry with exponential backoff. Silent failures in the middle of a pipeline corrupt data and are hard to debug later.
For keyboard/mouse automation (PyAutoGUI, AutoHotKey), add randomized movement speed and path — most detection systems flag perfectly linear mouse movements as robotic.

Google Sheets + Apps Script is a surprisingly powerful (and free) automation layer for non-developers. It can pull data from any public API, send emails, and trigger webhooks without any infrastructure.

mobile_apps.description: iOS, Android, React Native, Flutter, app development, App Store, Play Store

tips.tip: React Native's new architecture (Fabric + JSI) eliminates the old bridge bottleneck for most use cases. If you're starting a new RN project in 2025, enable the new architecture from day one — retrofitting it onto a large existing codebase is painful.

App Store review times have improved significantly: most apps now get reviewed in 24–48 hours. However, apps with subscription IAP or mature content flags average 4–7 days. Submit at least 2 weeks before a planned launch to be safe.

For Flutter, use const constructors wherever possible. Flutter's architecture rebuilds entire widget subtrees and const widgets are automatically cached and reused without rebuild, which is the single biggest free performance win.

ASO (App Store Optimization) matters more than most developers realize. The app title and first 100 characters of the description are the highest-weight fields for App Store search ranking. Repeat your primary keyword in the title and at the very start of the description.

social_media_automation.description: Social media bots, scheduling, growth, LinkedIn, Twitter/X, Instagram, TikTok

tips.tip: Most social platform APIs rate-limit by account, not by IP. Distributing actions across multiple accounts on different IPs is less effective than simply slowing down actions per account. Match the action frequency to what a real human power-user would do.

LinkedIn's Sales Navigator has a much more generous API than the free tier, but the real workaround most people use is Sales Navigator's export-to-CSV feature combined with Apollo.io for enrichment, rather than any API at all.

Twitter/X accounts get harder action limits the newer they are. A 2-week-old account doing 50 follows per day will trigger a soft-ban; a 2-year-old account with consistent posting history can do 3–4x more before hitting limits.

For Instagram automation, the web interface has stricter detection than the mobile API endpoints. Libraries that mimic the official iOS app's HTTP signature are significantly harder to flag than headless browser approaches.

api_development.description: REST APIs, GraphQL, webhooks, backend development, Node.js, Python, integrations

tips.tip: Webhook reliability requires idempotency. Your endpoint will receive duplicate deliveries — sometimes 5–10 minutes apart. Add a unique event ID check before processing any webhook payload to prevent double-charges or duplicate records.

For rate-limited third-party APIs, implement a token bucket in Redis rather than a simple per-minute counter. Token buckets allow bursting within limits and distribute requests more evenly, which keeps you under rate limits while maximizing throughput.

When integrating with Stripe, always validate the webhook signature using Stripe's SDK rather than accepting all POST requests to your endpoint. Unverified webhook endpoints are a common target for replay attacks.

GraphQL N+1 queries are the single most common performance killer in production GraphQL APIs. Use DataLoader (or any batching library) to batch and cache database calls per request cycle. Without it, a single list query can make hundreds of DB round-trips.

ai_ml.description: AI tools, LLMs, prompting, fine-tuning, automation with AI, ChatGPT, Claude

tips.tip: System prompts are the highest-leverage part of any LLM integration. Give the model a role, constraints, output format, and 2–3 concise in-context examples all in the system prompt. User prompt should only contain the variable data. This alone cuts hallucinations by 50–70% vs. putting everything in one big message.

For production AI pipelines, always add JSON output validation. LLMs occasionally produce near-valid JSON (trailing comma, missing brace). Parse errors in the middle of a pipeline are expensive — wrap every JSON.parse in a fallback strip-and-retry.

GPT-4o mini is remarkably capable for structured tasks (classification, extraction, JSON output) at roughly 1/30th the price of GPT-4o. Profile your prompts: classification and short-form tasks rarely need the full model.

RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) with a vector database is overkill for most use cases under ~100 documents. A well-structured JSON file loaded into the context window is faster, cheaper, and more reliable for small knowledge bases.

affiliate_marketing.description: Affiliate marketing, CPA, content sites, niches, monetization

tips.tip: Affiliate link cloaking with redirect tracking (e.g. PrettyLinks, ThirstyAffiliates, or a simple 301 on your own domain) gives you click analytics AND prevents affiliate ID stripping by ad blockers and browsers that strip UTM params from referral URLs.

Email list monetization consistently outperforms display ads by 10–50x RPM on the same traffic. Even a 500-person niche list monetized with a single relevant affiliate product outperforms a 5000-visitor/month content site on AdSense.

For CPA offers, the landing page split tests that usually move the needle most are: headline rewrites, hero image/video changes, and social proof placement (above or below CTA). Button color changes rarely produce statistically significant lifts.

discord_bots.description: Discord bots, Discord.js, bot development, community management, Discord API

tips.tip: Discord's Gateway intents system requires you to declare which events your bot needs. Using GUILD_MEMBERS or MESSAGE_CONTENT intents requires privileged intent approval in the developer portal for bots in 100+ servers. Plan for this before launch.

For high-traffic Discord bots, shard from day one even if you're small. Resharding a live bot is painful. Discord.js's built-in ShardingManager handles this automatically — the overhead on a small bot is negligible.

Discord slash commands are now the standard and soon the only supported interaction model. If you're still using message prefix commands, migrate — prefix commands require the MESSAGE_CONTENT privileged intent which is being restricted.

traffic_generation.description: Web traffic, paid ads, organic growth, Reddit, forum marketing, content distribution

tips.tip: Reddit's algorithm heavily weights early upvotes within the first 30–60 minutes for new posts. The best organic strategy is consistently posting value content in smaller, highly relevant subreddits where you'll appear in the top posts rather than competing in massive subreddits.

Content repurposing is more efficient than content creation. One long-form article → LinkedIn article excerpt → Twitter thread → short YouTube video → Quora answer. Five traffic channels from one piece of research.

For paid traffic, always separate warm (retargeting) and cold (prospecting) campaigns into different ad sets with different bids and creatives. Most ad accounts underperform because conversion events from retargeting inflate the apparent performance of cold campaigns.

general_development.description: Software development best practices, tools, debugging, deployment, version control

tips.tip: The most underused debugging technique is binary search: cut your code in half, confirm which half contains the bug, then cut again. This finds almost any non-obvious bug in O(log n) steps regardless of codebase size.

Environment variables vs config files: never commit secrets to git, even in private repos. Use a .env file locally and environment variables in production. Tools like dotenv (Node), python-decouple (Python), or just os.environ work fine for most use cases.

PM2 is still the simplest production process manager for Node.js on a VPS. cluster_mode + watch + max_restarts gives you auto-restart, multi-core utilization, and deployment in a single JSON config file with no Docker needed for most use cases.

Git commits should be atomic: one logical change per commit. The fastest way to untangle a messy git history when debugging a regression is git bisect — it binary searches through your commit history to find the exact commit that introduced a bug.
